notes: Steven Piano now keeps itself up to date: a new version shows on the Piano tab, and on the school tablet it installs without a tap. Share diagnostics sends the app's logs when something goes wrong.

Channels play your library without end: Calm, Epic, Baroque, Romantic, Impressionist, Nocturnes, Études and Everything, each at its own volume. Popular, Recognisable and Epic on piano fill themselves from your pieces. Left alone for a minute, the tablet becomes a display for passers-by. Every piece starts after a short pause, the score lights the notes it plays in yellow, a mini player (a now-playing panel on tablets) keeps the piece in sight, the controls float on frosted glass, the Piano tab's settings are grouped into pages, and Appearance can follow the system or stay light or dark.

Web control: open the panel in any browser on your Tailscale network to see what is playing, play and queue pieces, browse the library, start channels, adjust the piano, and add pieces by dropping MIDI or zip files onto the page. Guests can request a piece by scanning the printable poster, one request every five minutes, with an approve-first switch. Turn it on under Piano › Remote control and set a six-digit PIN. Also: hardening from the security audit of the panel, a larger title on the standby screen, and small fixes.

Firmware updates from the app: Piano › Firmware and status shows the piano's firmware version, checks for a signed release, and sends it over Bluetooth — the piano goes quiet, receives the image, verifies the signature, restarts, and rolls back by itself if the new firmware fails to start. Needs firmware 2.0.0 on the piano first (one USB flash).

Kiosk mode for the school tablet: with the app as device owner, Piano › Kiosk makes the app the home screen and switches off Home, Recents, the shade and the lock screen; the tablet comes straight back into the app after a reboot. Hold the byline for three seconds and enter the PIN to unlock for a while or turn kiosk off. In kiosk, settings, disconnecting, imports and deletions ask for the PIN; playing, queueing and browsing stay free. Left alone, the tablet rests in display mode.

Schedules: Piano › Schedule plays a channel, a playlist or a piece on chosen days at a set time, until an end time or the end, at its own volume. The tablet wakes for it even with the screen off, connects to the piano and starts; a missed start is shown on the page. The web panel edits the same schedules, and a channel's long-press can schedule it. Also: firmware-update progress stays visible in kiosk, and button labels are consistent.

Studio: the tablet can transcribe a piano recording into a playable piece and compose new piano pieces by itself, both running on the tablet with no cloud service. Piano › Studio downloads the two models once (125 MB and 173 MB). Transcribe a recording… takes any audio the tablet plays; Compose a piece… takes a mood, key, tempo, length and a piece from your library to write in the manner of. Each result asks Keep or Discard after your first listen. Also: the app keeps its other device architectures, the security audit's hardening, and a denser composing budget.

The resting screen now shows the album art with the piece's title, composer and a few lines about it, and fades in and out slowly; Piano › Display › Standby shows lets you keep the paper roll instead.

Piano sound on the tablet: real recordings of an upright piano play what the app plays, with a volume control on Now playing and under Piano › Playback › Tablet sound — by default only while the piano isn't connected, or always if you choose. The sound file (57 MB, CC0) downloads once. The resting screen credits Wikipedia under a piece's notes.

Liquid Glass across the app: the headers, the tab bar and rail, the mini player, the transport, sheets, menus and dialogs are frosted surfaces the content scrolls under, with a soft fade where content meets a bar; the play control is a solid circle again; on the tablet the transport yields its blur while the library scrolls. Reduce transparency or high contrast text gives solid surfaces.

Steven Piano Cloud: the web panel from anywhere over HTTPS, without Tailscale. Piano › Remote control › CLOUD enrols the tablet with a code from the console, and the panel then lives at https://<relay>/p/<piano>/ behind the same PIN as before; the console (on Steven's own Cloudflare account, behind Cloudflare Access) lists every piano with its live dot and what it plays, and offers play, pause, next, stop, channels, the guest switches, Load the library, Rotate secret, Revoke and Forget, with an audit log. Steven's library: Load Steven's library on the empty Library and in the + sheet downloads 1,726 pieces (60 MB) from GitHub, checked against its hash, after a note on the licences; Update the library later adds only pieces never offered before. On the tablet, glass menus now stay inside their pane.

Uploads become playlists. A zip or a folder is now a playlist named after it, its artist folders become the pieces' artists, and it lists first: Playlists sort newest first, with a button to switch to by name. Artists get their photographs from Wikipedia, bands and singers included, and a piece without one keeps its roll card. Songs uploaded before this update are repaired on the first launch: grouped into a playlist, with their artists filled in. Loose files dropped on the web panel go into Uploads, and the panel's Add tab says which playlist an upload went to, with a button to open it.

Keyboards. Connect a Bluetooth MIDI piano or a USB MIDI keyboard under Piano › Keyboard and play the piano live from it: on the Keys tab switch Live on, and the keys you press light up on screen and sound on the piano. Record what you play with the Record button; after Stop choose Keep and the take joins the new Recordings playlist. The app can also play its library on any MIDI piano, by Bluetooth or cable (Piano › Instrument › Another MIDI piano). For safety the keys and pedal are let go whenever the keyboard disconnects, Live is switched off or the app leaves the Keys screen. In kiosk mode Live and Record are free, and choosing an instrument or keyboard asks for the PIN.

Studio is now its own tab: type an idea such as "calm and slow" or "a bright waltz, 2 minutes" and the tablet writes a piece, showing each step, the notes as they are written and the time left. Every piece gets a cover drawn from its music and joins the new Made in Studio playlist; "another like it", "slower" or "longer" change the last one. On Now playing, drag the divider between the sheet music and the notes to resize them or hide one, and a View button holds the note style, fingering, chord names and hand colours. The Piano tab is reorganised into Instruments, The piano, Playing, Sharing and This tablet, with a search box that finds any setting by name.

The web panel now shows what the tablet shows: on Now playing, the sheet music with the notes turning yellow as they sound and the moving paper roll or falling notes with the keyboard strip, in step with the piano. Drag the divider between them, turn pages or tap a bar to jump there, and use View for the note style, fingering, chord names and hand colours. On a phone, pick Art, Notes or Score. It works over Tailscale, Wi-Fi and the internet link. The app also moves more smoothly: screens fade between tabs, buttons respond to touch, lists ease in, numbers roll, progress glides and menus grow from where you tapped. All of it is cut when the tablet's "remove animations" setting is on.

Studio's create box now sits in the middle of the screen under "What should the piano play?", with the aura moving and glowing around it. The piece being made shows under the box, and everything made before is behind the new History button and in the Made in Studio playlist. Channels gain Recognisable and Popular, each playing its list without end.

The Library now sorts music into Classical and Modern. A switch at the top (All · Classical · Modern) that search, pieces, playlists, composers, favorites and recent all follow; long-press a piece or an artist to move it to the other side. Two new channels, Classical and Modern, play a whole genre without end, and schedules can use them. The web panel's library has the same switch, and the guests' request page gets it too, with a search box and your modern songs to ask for. Studio understands "modern" and "classical" in a typed idea. Every recording now gets its own cover, Recordings and Made in Studio show covers instead of letters, keeping a recording says "Kept in Recordings.", and nothing the tablet makes itself shows an import message any more.

Every piece now gets its real album cover from Apple's catalogue when the title and artist clearly match; long-press a piece for Change cover. While a piece plays, the album's colours drift softly behind the player on Now playing and on the resting screen, like Apple Music; turn it off and on in Now playing's View menu or on Piano › Display. The web panel and your phone stay signed in for a year after one PIN.

Fast repeated notes now sound: the app lifts a key early so every strike can land, and repeats faster than the piano can manage keep the pulse instead of going silent. New rows on Piano › Playback: Re-strike time (Auto takes the piano's own figure), Dynamic range, Quietest note, and Expression, on by default at Light, which shapes loudness and timing as a pianist would: melody above accompaniment, phrases that swell and settle, downbeats that lean, chords that roll. Dynamics are heard with Full power off on Sound and touch; the page says so. Now playing shows the small album art beside the title.

The web panel shows its pictures over the internet link. Covers and portraits now load only for the rows in sight, a few at a time, wait and try again when the link is busy, and are kept by the browser for good, so Now playing and Up next show their art instead of empty tiles. Rows get a small picture instead of the large one, about a tenth of the data. Album covers also match a little wider: a film or game theme takes its soundtrack's cover, classical movements match by the work, and pieces that found nothing before are looked up once more.

The web panel has a new look: dark by default, a glass side rail, a big cover on Now playing with the album's colours as soft glows across the page, and Library as a grid of covers. Settings now holds the app's Playback settings beside the piano's pages. A new System page shows the tablet's battery, temperature, memory, storage and Wi-Fi, the piano's controller and power boards, what the app is running, a chart of the day, and tools: read status, find missing covers, reconnect the piano, all keys off, download diagnostics. The same System page is in the tablet app, first under This tablet on the Piano tab. On the tablet, Now playing has a big cover and a new Art only view beside the score and the notes. Find a cover, in a piece's menu on the panel, searches Apple's catalogue so you can choose a cover by hand or remove a wrong one. Phones get a bar at the foot with a More sheet. Covers load faster over the internet link.
